images.title: Shared primes of 45 and 75
images.purpose: Show that the common factors of 45 and 75 come from the primes they share, and the largest common subpart is the HCF.
images.composition: One two circle Venn diagram fills the centre of the frame with large prime digits; one result line sits below with white space all round.
exact_structure: Left circle outlined teal #0072B2, labelled 45 above it; right circle outlined amber #E69F00, labelled 75 above it; the circles overlap in the middle.
Overlap region, shaded light reddish purple #CC79A7: two primes, 3 and 5.
Exactly 4 prime digits in the diagram: 3, 3, 5, 5 (left side holds 3 × 3 × 5 = 45, right side holds 3 × 5 × 5 = 75).
rejection: the overlap holding anything other than one 3 and one 5
more or fewer than 4 prime digits in the diagram
images.takeaway: The primes in the overlap give the common factors, and their product is the HCF.
images.description: A Venn diagram with 3 only in 45, 3 and 5 shared, and 5 only in 75, above HCF = 3 × 5 = 15.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on common subparts of 45 and 75.
images.teaching_notes: Check that each circle multiplies back to its number, then read the shared part.

image_decisions.why: A Venn diagram of primes shows the shared part that gives the HCF.
